title: Coverage Determination Conditions, Homeowner Service Contracts
content:
A failure reported under a Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contract is covered only when every condition below holds; otherwise the determination is "not covered" with the first failing reason in this order.

| Order | Reason when it fails | Condition that must hold |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | contract not in force | the contract was active on the request date |
| 2 | waiting period | the failure was first reported on or after the coverage effective date; for an item or a higher limit added by a mid-term upgrade, also the upgrade waiting period below |
| 3 | item not in plan | the tier's cap for the covered item is greater than 0.00 |
| 4 | pre-existing condition | the failure did not arise from a condition that existed before the coverage effective date; known or visually detectable pre-existing conditions are never covered, and unknown, undetectable pre-existing conditions are covered only when the tier covers them |
| 5 | improper installation | a failure caused by improper prior installation, prior repair or a code violation in the original installation is covered only when the tier covers improper installation |
| 6 | misuse or external damage | failures from misuse, abuse, pests, weather, fire, flood or other external causes are never covered |
| 7 | cosmetic only | defects that do not affect operation are never covered |
| 8 | cap exhausted | the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit under the benefit cap rules are both above zero |

Conditions 1 to 3 and 8 are decided from the contract, request and payment records and may be determined without a dispatch; conditions 4 to 7 are decided from the dispatched contractor's diagnosis.

**Upgrade waiting period.** For an item or a higher limit added by a mid-term upgrade, the failure must also be first reported at least the upgrade waiting period (calendar days) after the upgrade takes effect; the count starts the day after the last plan change date and the boundary day itself qualifies. Until then such an item is determined under the prior tier, and an item that tier did not cover fails with "waiting period".

*Boundary pair, hypothetical, 30-day upgrade waiting period, upgrade effective April 10:* a failure first reported May 10 (day 30) meets the condition; one first reported May 9 (day 29) is determined under the prior tier.

**Stages.** An initial determination is issued once per service request. After a second opinion, one review determination is issued on the original request; the review outcome replaces the initial outcome and any authorization follows the review outcome.

### Worked reading (hypothetical)

A request on a contract that was active on the request date, reported after the coverage effective date, for an item whose cap on the tier is 0.00: conditions 1 and 2 hold, condition 3 fails, so the determination is "not covered — item not in plan", whatever the diagnosis would show on conditions 4 to 8.
